situation.s28_fremont_private_request.te: Lincoln asks Frémont to bring the emancipation paragraph of his proclamation within the August confiscation law. He asks Frémont to make the change himself.
situation.s28_fremont_private_request.in: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_fremont_private_request.op: Ask Frémont to modify the emancipation paragraph.
situation.s28_fremont_public_order.title: The public modification
situation.s28_fremont_public_order.text: Lincoln reports receiving Frémont’s preference for a public order and directs that the emancipation clause conform to the August confiscation law.
situation.s28_fremont_public_order.inact: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_fremont_public_order.optio: Publish the order limiting the emancipation clause.
situation.s28_maryland_arrest_instructio: Cameron directs Banks to prevent a secession act by the Maryland legislature and authorizes arrests if necessary. This is Cameron’s instruction; it does not establish that the legislature had agreed to secede.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
Direct Banks to prevent the act, with arrests if necessary.
situation.s28_compensated_emancipation_o: Lincoln proposes federal aid to a state that chooses gradual abolition of slavery. His message asks for congressional support and leaves acceptance to each state.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
Ask Congress to support aid for a state choosing gradual abolition.
situation.s28_hunter_revocation.title: Hunter’s declaration
situation.s28_hunter_revocation.text: Lincoln declares void the purported declaration of freedom printed under Hunter’s name. He reserves to himself the question of exercising that power. His paper says the government has not yet received authentic information that Hunter’s document is genuine.
situation.s28_hunter_revocation.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_hunter_revocation.option.r: Declare the proclamation void and reserve the question.
situation.s28_confiscation_bill.title: The confiscation bill and resolution
situation.s28_confiscation_bill.text: Lincoln’s message says he has approved the confiscation bill with its explanatory resolution. It also transmits the objections he prepared before learning that the resolution had passed. The separate Militia Act is not this bill.
situation.s28_confiscation_bill.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_confiscation_bill.option.s: Approve the confiscation bill with its explanatory resolution.
situation.s28_confiscation_bill.option.v: Return the confiscation bill with the prepared objections.
situation.s28_july_emancipation_draft.te: Lincoln’s draft announces his intention to recommend aid for gradual abolition and declares future freedom for people enslaved in states where federal authority remains unrecognized. This paper is a draft submitted to the cabinet.
situation.s28_july_emancipation_draft.in: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_july_emancipation_draft.op: Issue the proclamation drafted for the cabinet.
situation.s28_greeley_reply.title: Lincoln’s reply to Greeley
situation.s28_greeley_reply.text: Lincoln answers Greeley’s public letter by stating that his official object is to save the Union. He makes policy on slavery depend on that object and repeats his personal wish that all people could be free.
situation.s28_greeley_reply.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_greeley_reply.option.union: Send the reply stating the Union as the object of official policy.
situation.s28_preliminary_emancipation.t: The proclamation announces freedom on 1 January for people enslaved in states or parts then in rebellion and directs enforcement of existing return prohibitions. Welles records Blair’s objection to publication at this time, based on his fears about the border states and political opposition.
situation.s28_preliminary_emancipation.i: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_preliminary_emancipation.o: Withhold publication at this time because of the political risks.
situation.s28_august_arrest_order.title: Stanton’s arrest order
situation.s28_august_arrest_order.text: Stanton directs marshals and police officials to arrest people discouraging enlistment or engaging in the practices his order calls disloyal. He requires an immediate report for military commission proceedings. The order is not evidence that any particular person is guilty.
situation.s28_august_arrest_order.inacti: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_august_arrest_order.option: Issue Stanton’s order against discouraging enlistments.
situation.s28_september_habeas.title: The September suspension
situation.s28_september_habeas.text: Lincoln’s proclamation subjects the specified conduct to martial law and suspends habeas corpus for people held by military authority within the scope it states. Its description of conduct is a government allegation, not proof against an individual.
situation.s28_september_habeas.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_september_habeas.option.na: Issue the suspension and military-jurisdiction proclamation.
situation.s28_railroad_instructions.text: Halleck directs that orders to Haupt’s subordinates pass through Haupt and that train operations are not to be interfered with. Orders come from Pope or Halleck, with consultation of the nearest commander if the road is attacked.
situation.s28_railroad_instructions.inac: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_railroad_instructions.opti: Keep railroad instructions in Haupt’s chain of command.
situation.s28_cs_kentucky_neutrality.tex: Walker orders the troops withdrawn from Kentucky. Polk tells Davis he intends to retain Columbus, arguing that its occupation is necessary to protect western Tennessee. Davis replies that the necessity justifies the action. Polk’s account of local support is his claim.
situation.s28_cs_kentucky_neutrality.opt: Direct the troops to withdraw from Kentucky.
situation.s28_cs_kentucky_neutrality.ina: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_kentucky_application.te: Davis submits the provisional government’s application to Congress and asks its advice before negotiations. He argues for recognition despite the irregular proceedings. His assertion of majority support is his political claim, not an established vote or a transfer of the state.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_missions.te: Davis reports that commissioners have been sent to seek recognition and commercial treaties in Europe, with no intelligence from them yet received. He asks for appropriations for diplomatic agents to the independent American states.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_missions.op: Ask Congress to fund agents to the independent American states.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_missions.in: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_blockade_representation: Davis says evidence has been collected to challenge the blockade’s effectiveness and proposes laying it before foreign governments willing to hear it. His message seeks recognized diplomatic relations and says no offensive or defensive alliance has been proposed.
Instruct the agents to present the evidence against the blockade.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_danville_link.title: The Danville connection
situation.s28_cs_danville_link.text: Davis asks Congress to aid the company building the link between Danville and Greensboro. He presents the connection as a military necessity and distinguishes that argument from aid for a purely commercial work.
situation.s28_cs_danville_link.option.re: Ask Congress to aid completion of the Danville connection.
situation.s28_cs_danville_link.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_inspection_report.title: The requested inspection report
situation.s28_cs_inspection_report.text: Davis tells the House that the requested Jackson report has not reached the War Department. He says Lay’s report was made without inspecting the army at Romney and declines to communicate it, citing the public interest and the usual confidentiality of inspections.
situation.s28_cs_inspection_report.optio: Withhold Lay’s inspection report from the House.
situation.s28_cs_inspection_report.inact: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_mobile_defense.title: Mallory’s Mobile proposal
situation.s28_cs_mobile_defense.text: Davis submits Mallory’s plan for defending Mobile Bay and the Alabama River. He recommends an appropriation and proposes Navy procedures for disbursing it if Congress adopts the plan.
situation.s28_cs_mobile_defense.option.r: Request the appropriation for Mallory’s defense plan.
situation.s28_cs_mobile_defense.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_ironclad_opportunity.te: Davis recommends the appropriation requested for buying or constructing ironclad vessels. He doubts whether conditions in Europe will allow the proposed purchase and wants the Navy able to act if an opportunity appears.
situation.s28_cs_ironclad_opportunity.op: Request funds so the Navy can act if an opportunity appears.
situation.s28_cs_ironclad_opportunity.in: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_james_defenses.title: The James River defenses
situation.s28_cs_james_defenses.text: Davis generally agrees with the engineer report. He favors completing the river works and resists taking heavy guns from places where he thinks them more needed. He says fortifications can gain time but cannot by themselves save an army shut inside a city.
situation.s28_cs_james_defenses.option.c: Complete the existing works and keep guns where they are more needed.
situation.s28_cs_james_defenses.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_mississippi_floating_de: Davis forwards the Acting Secretary of War’s explanation of the million dollars already appropriated for floating defenses of the western waters. He asks Congress for an additional half-million dollars for the same purpose.
Ask Congress for the additional half-million dollars.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_proposal.t: Davis asks Congress to replace conflicting recruitment laws with a general system requiring military service from residents aged eighteen to thirty-five who are liable and not legally exempt. He argues that the burden should not fall only on volunteers.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_proposal.o: Ask Congress for the general enrollment law.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_proposal.i: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_act.title: The April conscription act
situation.s28_cs_conscription_act.text: The act authorizes calling resident white men aged eighteen to thirty-five who are not legally exempt for three years, unless the war ends sooner. It extends service for specified men already in the army and provides for reorganization and elections. Authority to call men is separate from their enrollment or arrival.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_amendments: Davis asks Congress to preserve state organizations offered for transfer, clarify the competing promotion clauses, and let re-enlisted volunteers serve in organizations they prefer. These are proposed amendments following the April act.
Request authority to accept the states’ existing organizations.
Ask Congress to clarify elections and promotion from the ranks.
Ask Congress to preserve re-enlisted volunteers’ choice of organization.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_georgia_organizations.t: Randolph’s 16 April instruction sends men who do not volunteer into existing companies. Brown asks to preserve the state troops’ organization and elections. On 17 April Davis tells Brown to retain the present organization because the emergency does not permit disorganization.
situation.s28_cs_georgia_organizations.o: Keep the state troops in their present organization for the emergency.
Assign men who do not volunteer to companies already in service.
situation.s28_cs_georgia_organizations.i: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_april_exemptions.title: The April exemptions
situation.s28_cs_april_exemptions.text: The exemption act lists public officials and specified occupations, including transport workers, ministers and teachers. It leaves findings of unfitness to rules of the Secretary of War and allows him to exempt factory superintendents and operatives within the specified class.
situation.s28_cs_conscription_extension_: Davis asks Congress to provide for a possible extension of conscription to ages thirty-five to forty-five. He presents this as preparation for an emergency that could arise while Congress is away, rather than a report that the new call has already been made.
Ask Congress for authority to call men aged thirty-five to forty-five.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_september_conscription_: The September act authorizes calls of resident white men aged thirty-five to forty-five who are not exempt. It directs that a partial call begin with the younger ages in that range and gives the President power to suspend execution where it is impracticable. It does not establish that every eligible man has been called or enrolled.
situation.s28_cs_october_exemption_act.t: Congress replaces the April exemptions with a revised list. Alongside occupational exemptions, the act exempts specified white men to police plantations and control enslaved people, including the provision based on twenty enslaved people. These exemptions preserve that system of control. The act’s stated conditions do not show who received an exemption.
situation.s28_cs_maryland_offensive.text: Lee argues that the moment favors entering Maryland. He reports poor equipment, weak transport and men without shoes, and warns that ammunition is his greatest concern. He asks that Richmond’s defenses be improved while the opposing army is occupied on this frontier. His estimates of the enemy are his intelligence.
situation.s28_cs_maryland_offensive.opti: Support Lee’s proposed movement into Maryland.
Direct improvements to Richmond’s land and river defenses.
situation.s28_cs_maryland_offensive.inac: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_offensive_disapproval_w: Lee asks for disapproval if opposed

Lee says he will move into Maryland at once unless Davis disapproves. He proposes entering Pennsylvania if the results justify it and unless Davis objects on political or other grounds. His letter does not report that either proposed movement has already succeeded.
Let Lee proceed with the movement he proposes.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_richmond_habeas.title: The Richmond suspension
situation.s28_cs_richmond_habeas.text: Davis’s proclamation extends martial law over Richmond and the surrounding ten miles. It suspends habeas corpus and civil jurisdiction except the mayor’s jurisdiction. Winder is charged with execution of the published proclamation.
Issue the Richmond suspension with the stated exception.
situation.s28_cs_richmond_habeas.inactio: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_east_tennessee_habeas.t: Davis extends martial law and suspends habeas corpus in the Department of East Tennessee. The proclamation preserves the enumerated civil business, including probate and administration of estates, while charging the department commander with its execution.
situation.s28_cs_east_tennessee_habeas.o: Issue the East Tennessee suspension with its civil exceptions.
situation.s28_cs_east_tennessee_habeas.i: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_vessel_veto.title: The proposed experimental vessel
situation.s28_cs_vessel_veto.text: Davis returns the vessel bill without approval. He says it would compel construction despite three unfavorable examinations and recommends keeping available effort and material on designs the Navy considers established. He reports the examiners’ judgment rather than proving the proposed vessel could not work.
situation.s28_cs_vessel_veto.option.retu: Return the vessel bill without approval.
situation.s28_cs_vessel_veto.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_hunter_sustain.title: Chase asks that Hunter’s order stand
situation.s28_hunter_sustain.text: Chase writes that he cannot judge Hunter’s military necessity from Washington, but urges Lincoln not to revoke the order freeing enslaved people. He recommends allowing it to stand on the commander’s responsibility as a military measure. His prediction of broad support is his assessment.
situation.s28_hunter_sustain.option.let-: Let Hunter’s order stand on his responsibility as commander.
situation.s28_hunter_sustain.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_vicksburg_inquiry.title: An inquiry to Vicksburg
situation.s28_cs_vicksburg_inquiry.text: Davis asks Smith about progress on the Arkansas, the condition of the Vicksburg defenses, and what aid can be given. He says that disasters above and below have increased the position’s value. The inquiry does not supply Smith’s answer.
situation.s28_cs_vicksburg_inquiry.optio: Ask Smith for the condition of the defenses and the aid he needs.
situation.s28_cs_vicksburg_inquiry.inact: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_kentucky_support_reques: Smith asks for support in Kentucky

Smith reports that supplies near Barboursville are nearly exhausted. He has chosen an advance toward Lexington over falling back into East Tennessee. He urges Davis to order Marshall through Pound Gap and asks for reinforcements and arms when practicable. His estimates of the enemy, local support and possible results are his own.
Seek Marshall’s advance and send reinforcements and arms when practicable.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_french_commercial_autho: Benjamin tells Slidell that Davis would approve a treaty allowing French products duty-free entry for a defined period if it induced France to stop acquiescing in the blockade. After cautious inquiry, Slidell may also negotiate a subsidy if it would remove an obstacle. These are conditional permissions to negotiate; no French agreement is reported.
Authorize negotiation of the conditional commercial concession.
Permit subsidy negotiations after the specified inquiry.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_priority.te: Benjamin authorizes Slidell to use the means allowed for seeking relief from the blockade to obtain recognition instead, if he finds recognition more feasible. Benjamin predicts that recognition would hasten peace. That prediction does not establish a foreign decision or a peace settlement.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_priority.op: Authorize Slidell to pursue recognition if it is more feasible.
situation.s28_cs_recognition_priority.in: No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_cs_diplomatic_dispatch_rou: Benjamin asks Slidell to seek French permission for Confederate dispatches to travel through French dispatch vessels. He reports that the existing French service is restricted to French official correspondence and argues for an exception. No permission to carry Confederate dispatches has yet been reported in this letter.
Ask France to permit the dispatches through its service.
No answer to this paper has been sent.
situation.s28_fremont_sustain.title: Frémont defends the emancipation clause
situation.s28_fremont_sustain.text: Frémont tells Lincoln that he still considers the emancipation clause right and necessary. He argues that retracting it himself would imply that he thought it wrong or insufficiently considered. If Lincoln remains opposed, Frémont asks for an open direction to correct it. This facet concerns the emancipation clause.
situation.s28_fremont_sustain.option.ema: Leave the emancipation clause in place.
situation.s28_fremont_sustain.inaction: No answer to this paper has been sent.
